message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
My tentative reading is **sinus rhythm at about 90–95 beats/minute, with mild nonspecific ST–T changes**. Image quality and baseline movement limit precise measurements.

- **Rhythm:** Regular, with a P wave before each QRS—consistent with the heart’s normal pacemaker.
- **Conduction:** PR and QRS intervals appear within normal limits; no obvious bundle branch block.
- **Axis:** Appears normal.
- **ST/T waves:** Slight ST depression/flattening in the lateral chest leads, most noticeable around V4–V5. These changes are not specific enough to identify a cause.
- **No clear ST-elevation heart attack pattern** is visible.

This should be reviewed alongside symptoms and any previous ECG. An ECG alone cannot exclude a heart attack. If you currently have chest pressure, shortness of breath, sweating, or fainting, seek emergency care now. [NICE guidance](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/CG95/chapter/recommendations)

How old is the person, why was this ECG taken, and were there any symptoms?
